# mdshare — guide for AI agents

mdshare turns Markdown into a clean, readable web page. You POST Markdown, you get a URL.
New documents are PRIVATE: only the owner can open them until the owner (or a token with a
publish scope) makes them public. Unkept documents expire (default 24 hours, max 7 days).

## Publish

POST /api/share
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>        (optional; required for "keep")

{"markdown": "<the document>", "keep": true, "ttl": 86400, "parent": "<id>", "origin": "<where feedback goes>",
 "lang": "zh", "translation_of": "<id>", "collection": "<slug>"}

- markdown: required, max 100 KB.
- keep: true = never expires. Honoured for a valid token or the signed-in owner; ignored otherwise.
  Use it for anything the user will want later (reports, plans, explanations). Skip it for scratch.
- ttl: seconds until expiry when not kept (max 604800).
- parent: id of the document this one replaces (a revision). The old page then shows "a newer
  version exists" and the new one gets "What changed". Needs the owner or a token that can read the
  parent (documents:read, or it created the parent); otherwise 404 and nothing is created.
- origin: your session or chat id (letters, digits, : . @ / # + - _; max 200). Stored only for a
  token or the owner. Reader feedback on this document is listed with it, so it can be routed back.
- lang: "zh" or "en" (anything else is 400).
- translation_of: id of the same text in the other language. Both pages then show a 中文 / English
  switch (a reader sees it only when the other page is public too). The owner can link any two
  documents; a token only documents it created itself (the target and the original it belongs to;
  documents:read is not enough). Otherwise 404 and nothing is created, the same as a missing id.
  lang is detected when you leave it out; the same language as the target is 400.
- collection: a slug (1-48 of a-z 0-9 -, e.g. "glm-study"). The owner sees it at /c/<slug>: one
  row per document (newest version only, a zh/en pair as one row), with read status. Needs a token
  or the owner (ignored otherwise; "collection_ignored" says so). Invalid slug: 400.
  A new version (parent) keeps the parent's lang, translation_of and collection; a translation
  joins its original's collection.
Response: {"url", "id", "kept", "expires_in", "format_guide", "checks", "parent"?, "origin"?,
"lang"?, "translation_of"?, "collection"?, "keep_ignored"?}. Give the user the url. Read "checks" first: {"ok", "warnings": [{"rule",
"severity": "warn"|"info", "line", "message"}], "stats": {"minutes", "tables", "maxColumns", ...}}.
"warn" means the page will look broken (unclosed code block or :::block, a table row with extra
cells, a mermaid block that won't draw, a redaction placeholder, a local file link). Fix and
publish again with "parent" set to the broken id. "keep_ignored" explains a keep that didn't apply.

Other endpoints: POST /api/diagram {"svg", "title", "markdown"?, "keep"?} -> /d/<id>;
GET /api/pastes?q=<text>&kind=paste|diagram|archify lists the catalog (documents:read token).

## Read and search

Send the token as "Authorization: Bearer <token>" (not x-api-key, not ?key=: those are not read,
and a refused request says so in its hint). A 401 carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer, a "hint"
and this guide's URL.
GET /v/<id>   with Authorization: Bearer -> the stored Markdown (text/markdown), so a /v/ link
              someone gave you works as-is. GET /raw/<id> is the same (text/plain). Readable for
              the owner, a public doc, a documents:read token, or the token that created it.
              Anything else is 404 {"error", "hint"}, the same for a private id and a missing one.
GET /api/doc?action=search&q=<text>&limit=20&offset=0      full-text search (documents:read)
     q: 1-200 characters, matched literally and case-insensitively in titles and bodies (Chinese
     works: q=缓存命中). URL-encode it. Response: {"results": [{"id", "title", "snippet" (plain
     text around the first match), "created_at", "kept", "is_public", "url"}], "total",
     "next_offset"}. Title matches first, then newest; expired documents are not included.
     Read a hit with GET /v/<id>. CLI: mdshare-cli search "<text>" [--json];
     mdshare-cli read <id or link>. At most 60 searches a minute per token; past that 429 with
     Retry-After (seconds) and {"retry_after"}.
Token scopes: documents:read, documents:write, documents:publish (own docs), documents:publish:any,
activity:read (read receipts + feedback), activity:write (resolve feedback).
To publish (make public): PATCH /api/pin {"id", "kind": "paste", "is_public": true, "keep": true}.

## Your own account (beta)

POST /api/auth?action=signup {"label"?} -> 201 {"user_id", "token", "entry_url", "guide"}: a new,
empty library and a token (documents:read, documents:write, documents:publish). Do it once; save
the token; give entry_url (the person's private sign-in link) to them only. 403 {"error": "beta
full"}; 429 with Retry-After. POST /api/auth?action=entry-link with the token -> {"entry_url"}, a
new link (the old one stops working). Beta limits: 200 documents a day (429) and 512 KB each (413).

## Reading loop: did they read it, what did they ask for

The owner's opens and reader feedback are recorded; readers' (anyone else's) never are.
GET  /api/doc?action=reads&unread=1&days=7   documents the owner hasn't opened yet (activity:read)
GET  /api/doc?action=reads&ids=a,b          opens, last opened, max scroll %, active seconds
GET  /api/doc?action=feedback&status=open   open feedback: {id, doc_id, doc_title, origin, kind,
     quote, note, context: {heading, before, after}}. kind: example | unclear | wrong | expand | note
     (the reader selected `quote` and asked for an example / said it's unclear / wrong / wants more /
     wrote `note`).
POST /api/doc?action=resolve {"ids": ["fb_..."], "status": "resolved", "resolved_in": "<new id>"}
     after you publish the fix as a new version (activity:write).
GET  /api/doc?action=versions&id=<id>        the version chain, oldest first (documents:read).

## Translations and collections (link or file existing documents)

POST /api/doc?action=translation {"id", "translation_of": "<original id>" | null, "lang"?: "zh"|"en"}
     links (or with null unlinks) the document's whole version family. Needs documents:write or
     documents:publish, on a document this token created, linked to a target it created too (the
     owner: any pair). Otherwise 404, the same for a missing id.
POST /api/doc?action=collection {"id", "collection": "<slug>" | null}   same rules; whole family.
GET  /api/doc?action=collection                every collection: [{"slug", "count", "updated_at"}]
GET  /api/doc?action=collection&slug=<slug>    its contents: {"items": [{"title", "id", "kept",
     "opened", "max_scroll", "updated_at", "links": [{"id", "lang", "version", "is_public"}]}]}
     (documents:read). The /c/<slug> page itself is owner-only; tokens get the sign-in page.
Every GET /api/doc action (search, collection, versions, reads, feedback) allows 60 calls a minute
per token, each action on its own; past that 429 with Retry-After (seconds) and {"retry_after"}.
CLI: mdshare-cli create paste f.md --lang zh --translation-of <id> --collection <slug>;
     mdshare-cli translate <id> --of <id>; mdshare-cli collection <id> <slug>; mdshare-cli collections [slug].
Answer feedback by revising the passage it quotes, not by rewriting the whole document.

## How to write a document that reads well

1. Start with one "# Title".
2. Put the answer first: a "## TL;DR" (or "## Summary", "## 结论", "## 一句话结论") section of
   1-3 sentences. It renders as a summary card at the top.
3. Use "##" for main sections (3+ sections get a contents sidebar and reading progress).
   A line that is only bold text ("**Key point**") renders as a small heading.
4. Prefer short paragraphs and lists. "- **Label**: explanation" renders as key-point rows.
   A numbered list where every item starts in bold renders as step cards.
5. Use tables for comparisons. Numeric columns are right-aligned; cells starting with ✅ ❌ ⚠️ are tinted. Wide tables are laid out automatically: they widen into free space, scroll with a fixed first column, and become cards on phones. Keep the first column a short row label. To force a view, wrap one table:
   :::table cards Optional caption      (options: cards | table | wide | compact; other words = caption)
   | ... table ... |
   :::
6. Use fenced code blocks with a language (```bash, ```python).
7. Draw a diagram (```mermaid) whenever a picture says it faster than prose, right next to the
   paragraph that explains it, the same way you'd use a table:
   - a process or pipeline with 4+ steps, or with branches/loops      -> flowchart LR / TD
   - who talks to whom, in what order (requests, handoffs, approvals) -> sequenceDiagram
   - how parts connect (architecture, data flow, money flow)          -> flowchart with subgraph
   - a timeline or plan                                               -> timeline or gantt
   - a hierarchy or breakdown                                         -> mindmap or flowchart TD
   Keep it to one idea and at most ~12 nodes; short labels (put the detail in the text); quote
   labels that contain punctuation: A["Score (0-1)"]. Chinese labels are fine. The text should
   still make sense without the picture. Diagrams use the page colours, scroll inside their frame
   on a phone, and have an Expand button. One that doesn't parse shows its source and is reported
   in "checks" when the type is wrong; preview locally to be sure it draws.
   Example:
   ```mermaid
   flowchart LR
     Q[Question] --> S[Search] --> R{Enough evidence?}
     R -- no --> S
     R -- yes --> W[Write answer]
   ```
8. Don't paste raw HTML; it is sanitised. Don't put the whole document in one code block.
9. Explain jargon in a glossary: a section titled exactly "## 术语表" (or 术语, 名词解释, 关键术语,
   Glossary, Terms, Key terms) whose bullets are all "- **TERM**：definition" (or "- **TERM**: ...").
   It renders as a card, and the FIRST time each term appears in the text it gets a dotted
   underline that shows the definition (hover, tap or keyboard). One bold label can hold several
   names: "- **TTS, Text-to-Speech（文本转语音）**：..." matches TTS, Text-to-Speech or 文本转语音.
10. End with a recap when the reader should keep something: make the LAST "##" section exactly
   "## 要点回顾" (or 记住这几点, 记住这三点, 关键要点, Key takeaways, Takeaways, Recap, What to remember)
   with 2-4 bullets. It renders as a recap card. "## 总结", "## Summary" and "## Conclusion" stay
   ordinary sections, and so does a recap heading that isn't the last section.

## Extra blocks (optional; all degrade to readable text elsewhere)

Callouts (GitHub alert syntax):
> [!NOTE] | [!TIP] | [!IMPORTANT] | [!WARNING] | [!CAUTION]
> Text of the callout.

A quote starting with "Note:", "Tip:", "Warning:", "注意：", "提示：" or "警告：" also becomes a callout.

Summary card with a custom label:
:::summary Bottom line
One or two sentences.
:::

Number cards (one per line, "value | label", optional {up} {down} {accent}):
:::stats
$140.6M | first-half revenue
+1,252% | year over year {up}
:::

Timeline ([x] = done):
:::steps
- [x] **Phase 1**: what happened
- [ ] **Phase 2**: what's next
:::

One step at a time (a procedure the reader follows): ":::steps reveal [caption]". Step 1 shows with
"Next step (2/N)" / "下一步 (2/N)" and "Show all" / "全部展开"; printing shows every step. A numbered
list whose items all start in bold becomes numbered step cards, any other list the timeline:
:::steps reveal First deploy
1. **Install** the CLI.
2. **Sign in** with your token.
3. **Publish** the file.
:::

Side-by-side comparison (each ### starts a column; the last is highlighted):
:::compare
### Before
- ...
### After
- ...
:::

Cards (:::cards, same ### structure) and tabs (:::tabs, each ### is a tab).
Callout with your own label: :::note Label / :::tip / :::warning / :::important / :::caution, closed by :::.

Inline: ==highlight==, :badge[shipped], :badge[blocked], :badge[beta]{blue}
(badge colors: green red amber blue accent gray; picked from the words if omitted).

Rules: blocks open with ":::name" at the start of a line and close with a line that is only ":::".
Blocks don't nest. Close every block you open. Unknown block names are shown as plain text.

Optional page settings, only as the very first lines:
---
accent: teal          (terracotta | amber | teal | indigo)
toc: false
layout: wide
tables: cards         (auto | table | cards | compact)
---

## Charts (```mermaid; drawn in the page colours, readable on a phone)

Pick the chart for the reader's question; put the numbers in the text too.
- bar or line: a number over time, or across a few groups -> xychart-beta (quote the x-axis labels;
  start the y-axis at 0 for bars; "bar" and "line" series can share one chart)
- pie: one whole split into 2-6 parts (more parts or exact comparison: use bars)
- quadrant: a few options placed on two scales (effort/impact) -> quadrantChart, coordinates 0-1;
  quadrant-1 is top right, 2 top left, 3 bottom left, 4 bottom right
- mindmap: a topic and its parts, 2-3 levels; indentation makes the levels
- timeline: dates or phases with 1-2 short events each
Chinese labels are fine (quote them in x-axis lists). Minimal correct examples:
```mermaid
xychart-beta
  title "Weekly readers"
  x-axis ["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4"]
  y-axis "Readers" 0 --> 500
  bar [120, 210, 340, 420]
  line [100, 190, 300, 390]
```
```mermaid
pie title Where the week went
  "Reading" : 45
  "Writing" : 30
  "Review" : 25
```
```mermaid
quadrantChart
  title Effort and impact
  x-axis Low effort --> High effort
  y-axis Low impact --> High impact
  quadrant-1 Plan it
  quadrant-2 Do it first
  quadrant-3 Skip it
  quadrant-4 Hand it off
  Glossary: [0.3, 0.8]
  Charts: [0.7, 0.75]
```
```mermaid
mindmap
  root((Reading))
    Formatting
      Summary card
    Charts
      Bars
```
```mermaid
timeline
  title Release plan
  section November
    Beta : 50 readers
  section December
    Launch : Public site : Pricing page
```

Human-readable version with rendered examples: /guide
